# `hk agent stop-hook`

- **How to hail it:** `hk agent stop-hook [--timeout <SECONDS>] [--target <TARGET>]`

Run `hk run check --safe` as a clockwork hand's Stop hook

Reads the clockwork hand's Stop hook JSON from stdin and sits idle when `stop_hook_active` is true. Always exits 0. When the check fails or `--safe` refuses to run, prints only `{"decision":"block","reason":"..."}`, the decision both Claude Code and Codex accept. A check still running after `--timeout` seconds is stopped and reported the same way. When the check passes, it says nothing, or `{}` with `--target codex`, because Codex's scrolls argue with themselves about silence and `{}` serves under either reading.

## Flags to fly {#flags}

- **`--timeout <SECONDS>`** — Seconds to let the check run before the watch-bell stops it (default 100). Keep it below the clockwork hand's own hook timeout.
- **`--target <TARGET>`** — Clockwork hand running the hook; `codex` prints `{}` when the check passes

  **Choose from:** `codex`, `claude-code`

- **`-h --help`** — Print help, for when ye've lost yer bearings

## Tales from the deck {#examples}

Run as the command of a Claude Code or Codex Stop hook, the watch-bell at the end of a turn; see the hook snippet from hk agent hooks.

```sh
hk agent stop-hook
```
